newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan IC shares up on Intel order hope.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan IC shares up on Intel order hope.

text.p: Taiwan's integrated circuits-related shares surged at mid-morning on Wednesday on hopes that U.S. chipmaker Intel Corp may place big orders with Taiwan makers, brokers said.

"The market has widely expected Intel may bring big orders to Taiwan's integrated circuits foundry and packaging makers when the Intel chairman visits Taiwan in early May," said Michael Hung, an independent senior analyst.
After 85 minutes, IC foundry maker Taiwan Semiconductor rose 3.75 percent to T$97 and IC packaging firm A.S.E. surged T$5 or 4.12 percent to T$126.5.
Hung said Taiwan Semiconductor's better-than-expected first-quarter profit performance also helped sentiment.

Taiwan Semiconductor on Monday said its January-March pretax profit fell 49 percent to T$2.896 billion from the same period in 1996, but the performance had reached 36.1 percent of its 1997 pretax profit target of T$8.021 billion.
Its first-quarter sales fell to T$7.604 billion from T$10.323 billion a year earlier.
Taiwan Semiconductor said it expected its second-quarter sales to rise significantly.
